answer: To resist sybil attacks, agent economies can require a two-stage proof of work. First, each identity must mine a fresh cryptographic puzzle, turning every new account into a costly lagoon of compute that farms cannot cheaply fill. Second, attestation weight comes only after peers verify a track record, so an attacker's ferrous swarm of inauthentic nodes stays weak. Established identities then serve as a trusted harbor that anchors the network, while sybil farms are priced out by cumulative effort.
